sanskrit: evam uktaḥ śubhaṃ vākyaṃ tāpasyā dharmasaṃhitam uvāca hanumān vākyaṃ tām aninditaceṣṭitām
english: Thus addressed by the auspicious, dharma-laden words of the female ascetic, Hanumān spoke his words to that woman of blameless conduct.

sanskrit: śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ prapannāḥ smaḥ sarve vai dharmacāriṇi yaḥ kṛtaḥ samayo 'smākaṃ sugrīveṇa mahātmanā sa tu kālo vyatikrānto bile ca parivartatām
english: "We have all taken refuge in you, O lady of righteous conduct. The time-limit set for us by the great-souled Sugrīva has passed, and we have been dwelling inside the cave."

sanskrit: sā tvam asmād bilād ghorād uttārayitum arhasi
english: "You yourself should rescue us from this dreadful cave."

sanskrit: tasmāt sugrīvavacanād atikrāntān gatāyuṣaḥ trātum arhasi naḥ sarvān sugrīvabhayaśaṅkitān
english: "Therefore please save all of us, who have overstepped Sugrīva's command, whose lives are as good as forfeit, and who are filled with dread of Sugrīva."

sanskrit: mahac ca kāryam asmābhiḥ kartavyaṃ dharmacāriṇi tac cāpi na kṛtaṃ kāryam asmābhir iha vāsibhiḥ
english: "There is also a great task that must be accomplished by us, O righteous lady, and that task too has not been done by us who have been dwelling here."

sanskrit: evam uktā hanumatā tāpasī vākyam abravīt jīvatā duṣkaraṃ manye praviṣṭena nivartitum
english: Thus addressed by Hanumān, the female ascetic spoke: "I think it is exceedingly difficult for any living being who has entered here to turn back."

sanskrit: tapasas tu prabhāvena niyamopārjitena ca sarvān eva bilād asmād uddhariṣyāmi vānarān
english: "But by the power of my austerities and by virtue of the self-discipline I have acquired, I shall draw all these monkeys out of this cave."

sanskrit: nimīlayata cakṣūṃṣi sarve vānarapuṃgavāḥ na hi niṣkramituṃ śakyam animīlitalocanaiḥ
english: "Close your eyes, all you bull-like monkeys. For it is not possible to emerge with eyes open."

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃmīlitāḥ sarve sukumārāṅgulaiḥ karaiḥ sahasā pidadhur dṛṣṭiṃ hṛṣṭā gamanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Then all of them, eager and desirous of departing, instantly covered their eyes with their soft-fingered hands and shut them tight.

sanskrit: vānarās tu mahātmāno hastaruddhamukhās tadā nimeṣāntaramātreṇa bilād uttāritās tayā
english: Those high-souled monkeys, their faces covered by their hands, were lifted out of the cave by her in the mere twinkling of an eye.

sanskrit: tatas tān vānarān sarvāṃs tāpasī dharmacāriṇī niḥsṛtān viṣamāt tasmāt samāśvāsyedam abravīt
english: Then the virtuous female ascetic, having brought all those monkeys forth from that treacherous place, reassured them and spoke thus.

sanskrit: eṣa vindhyo giriḥ śrīmān nānādrumalatāyutaḥ eṣa prasavaṇaḥ śailaḥ sāgaro 'yaṃ mahodadhiḥ
english: "This is the glorious Vindhya mountain, covered with many trees and creepers. This is the Prasavaṇa peak. And this is the ocean, the great sea."

sanskrit: svasti vo 'stu gamiṣyāmi bhavanaṃ vānararṣabhāḥ ity uktvā tad bilaṃ śrīmat praviveśa svayaṃprabhā
english: "May good fortune attend you; I will return to my abode, O bull-like monkeys." Having said this, Svayaṃprabhā entered that beautiful cave once more.

sanskrit: tatas te dadṛśur ghoraṃ sāgaraṃ varuṇālayam apāram abhigarjantaṃ ghorair ūrmibhir ākulam
english: Then they beheld the dreadful ocean, abode of Varuṇa, boundless and roaring loudly, churned by terrible waves.

sanskrit: mayasya māyā vihitaṃ giridurgaṃ vicinvatām teṣāṃ māso vyatikrānto yo rājñā samayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: While they had been searching through that mountain stronghold fashioned by Maya's magic, the month set as the time-limit by the king had passed.

sanskrit: vindhyasya tu gireḥ pāde saṃprapuṣpitapādape upaviśya mahābhāgāś cintām āpedire tadā
english: Sitting at the foot of the Vindhya mountain, beneath fully flowering trees, those great and fortunate ones then fell into anxious thought.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṣpātibhārāgrāṃl latāśatasamāvṛtān drumān vāsantikān dṛṣṭvā babhūvur bhayaśaṅkitāḥ
english: Then, seeing the springtime trees laden with blossoms at their crowns and encircled by hundreds of creepers, they became filled with fearful apprehension.

sanskrit: te vasantam anuprāptaṃ prativedya parasparam naṣṭasaṃdeśakālārthā nipetur dharaṇītale
english: Informing one another that spring had arrived, and recognizing that the time and purpose of their mission were lost, they sank down upon the ground.

sanskrit: sa tu siṃharṣabha skandhaḥ pīnāyatabhujaḥ kapiḥ yuvarājo mahāprājña aṅgado vākyam abravīt
english: Then Aṅgada, the crown prince, that great wise monkey with the shoulders of a lion and bull, with broad long arms, spoke.

sanskrit: śāsanāt kapirājasya vayaṃ sarve vinirgatāḥ māsaḥ pūrṇo bilasthānāṃ harayaḥ kiṃ na budhyate
english: "We all set out under the command of the monkey-king; a full month has passed while we were dwelling in the cave — do the monkeys not perceive this?"

sanskrit: tasminn atīte kāle tu sugrīveṇa kṛte svayam prāyopaveśanaṃ yuktaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca vanaukasām
english: "Now that the time-limit set by Sugrīva himself has expired, it is fitting for all of us forest-dwellers to undertake a fast unto death."

sanskrit: tīkṣṇaḥ prakṛtyā sugrīvaḥ svāmibhāve vyavasthitaḥ na kṣamiṣyati naḥ sarvān aparādhakṛto gatān
english: "Sugrīva is by nature harsh, and he is firm in his role as master; he will not pardon all of us who have transgressed and return before him."

sanskrit: apravṛttau ca sītāyāḥ pāpam eva kariṣyati tasmāt kṣamam ihādyaiva prāyopaviśanaṃ hi naḥ
english: "And without news of Sītā, he will surely do evil. Therefore it is proper for us to undertake a fast unto death right here today."

sanskrit: tyaktvā putrāṃś ca dārāṃś ca dhanāni ca gṛhāṇi ca yāvan na ghātayed rājā sarvān pratigatān itaḥ vadhenāpratirūpeṇa śreyān mṛtyur ihaiva naḥ
english: "Before the king slaughters all of us who have returned from here — having abandoned sons, wives, wealth, and homes — with a punishment beyond fitting, death here itself is better for us."

sanskrit: na cāhaṃ yauvarājyena sugrīveṇābhiṣecitaḥ narendreṇābhiṣikto 'smi rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: "Moreover, I was not consecrated as crown prince by Sugrīva; it was by Rāma, the lord of men, whose deeds are effortless, that I was consecrated."

sanskrit: sa pūrvaṃ baddhavairo māṃ rājā dṛṣṭvā vyatikramam ghātayiṣyati daṇḍena tīkṣṇena kṛtaniścayaḥ
english: "That king who bore enmity toward me before, seeing my transgression, will put me to death with a sharp punishment, his resolve fixed."

sanskrit: kiṃ me suhṛdbhir vyasanaṃ paśyadbhir jīvitāntare ihaiva prāyam āsiṣye puṇye sāgararodhasi
english: "What use are my friends witnessing my calamity at the moment of death? I shall sit here in fast unto death on this sacred shore of the ocean."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā kumāreṇa yuvarājena bhāṣitam sarve te vānaraśreṣṭhāḥ karuṇaṃ vākyam abruvan
english: Having heard these words spoken by the young crown prince, all those foremost monkeys spoke pitifully in reply.

sanskrit: tīkṣṇaḥ prakṛtyā sugrīvaḥ priyāsaktaś ca rāghavaḥ adṛṣṭāyāṃ ca vaidehyāṃ dṛṣṭvāsmāṃś ca samāgatān
english: "Sugrīva is by nature harsh, and Rāghava is ardently attached to his beloved; with Vaidehī not found, and seeing us return together —"

sanskrit: rāghavapriyakāmārthaṃ ghātayiṣyaty asaṃśayam na kṣamaṃ cāparāddhānāṃ gamanaṃ svāmipārśvataḥ
english: "— for Rāghava's sake and to please him, he will undoubtedly have us killed. And it is not proper for those who have transgressed to go before their master."

sanskrit: plavaṃgamānāṃ tu bhayārditānāṃ śrutvā vacas tāra idaṃ babhāṣe alaṃ viṣādena bilaṃ praviśya vasāma sarve yadi rocate vaḥ
english: Then Tāra, hearing the words of the terror-stricken monkeys, spoke thus: "Enough of despair. Let us all enter the cave and dwell there, if you agree."

sanskrit: idaṃ hi māyā vihitaṃ sudurgamaṃ prabhūtavṛkṣodakabhojyapeyam ihāsti no naiva bhayaṃ puraṃdarān na rāghavād vānararājato 'pi vā
english: "For this cave wrought by Maya's magic is most inaccessible; it has abundant trees, water, food, and drink. Here we need fear neither Indra, nor Rāghava, nor the monkey-king."

sanskrit: śrutvāṅgadasyāpi vaco 'nukūlam ūcuś ca sarve harayaḥ pratītāḥ yathā na hanyema tathāvidhānam asaktam adyaiva vidhīyatāṃ naḥ
english: Hearing even Aṅgada's favorable response, all the monkeys, encouraged, said: "Let a plan by which we shall not be slain be devised for us without delay, this very day."

sanskrit: tathā bruvati tāre tu tārādhipativarcasi atha mene hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ hanumān aṅgadena tat
english: While Tāra, who shone with the splendor of the lord of stars, spoke thus, Hanumān perceived that the kingdom was being seized by Aṅgada.

sanskrit: buddhyā hy aṣṭāṅgayā yuktaṃ caturbalasamanvitam caturdaśaguṇaṃ mene hanumān vālinaḥ sutam
english: Hanumān judged Vālin's son to be endowed with the eight qualities of intellect, possessed of the fourfold strength, and graced with fourteen royal virtues.

sanskrit: āpūryamāṇaṃ śaśvac ca tejobalaparākramaiḥ śaśinaṃ śuklapakṣādau vardhamānam iva śriyā
english: He saw him ever increasing in splendor, strength, and valor, growing in royal majesty like the moon waxing from the first night of the bright fortnight.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatisamaṃ buddhyā vikrame sadṛśaṃ pituḥ śuśrūṣamāṇaṃ tārasya śukrasyeva puraṃdaram
english: He was Bṛhaspati's equal in intellect, his father's equal in valor, and was attending upon Tāra as Śukra attends upon Indra.

sanskrit: bhartur arthe pariśrāntaṃ sarvaśāstraviśāradam abhisaṃdhātum ārebhe hanumān aṅgadaṃ tataḥ
english: Then Hanumān, perceiving him exhausted in his master's cause and skilled in all the sciences, began to address Aṅgada with persuasive words.

sanskrit: sa caturṇām upāyānāṃ tṛtīyam upavarṇayan bhedayām āsa tān sarvān vānarān vākyasaṃpadā
english: Describing the third of the four political means — dissension — he split apart all those monkeys with the excellence of his speech.

sanskrit: teṣu sarveṣu bhinneṣu tato 'bhīṣayad aṅgadam bhīṣaṇair bahubhir vākyaiḥ kopopāyasamanvitam
english: When all those monkeys had been thus divided, he then alarmed Aṅgada with many frightening words, employing the means of intimidation with anger.

sanskrit: tvaṃ samarthataraḥ pitrā yuddhe tāreya vai dhuram dṛḍhaṃ dhārayituṃ śaktaḥ kapirājyaṃ yathā pitā
english: "You, O son of Tārā, are more capable than your father in battle; you are able to bear the burden firmly and rule the monkey kingdom just as your father did."

sanskrit: nityam asthiracittā hi kapayo haripuṃgava nājñāpyaṃ viṣahiṣyanti putradārān vinā tvayā
english: "For monkeys are by nature fickle-minded, O bull among monkeys; without you they will not endure being commanded, apart from their sons and wives."

sanskrit: tvāṃ naite hy anuyuñjeyuḥ pratyakṣaṃ pravadāmi te yathāyaṃ jāmbavān nīlaḥ suhotraś ca mahākapiḥ
english: "These very ones — Jāmbavān, Nīla, and the great monkey Suhotra — would follow you; I tell you this plainly."

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ ta ime sarve sāmadānādibhir guṇaiḥ daṇḍena na tvayā śakyāḥ sugrīvād apakarṣitum
english: "Neither I nor all these others can be drawn away from Sugrīva by conciliation, gifts, or any other means — nor by force — except by you."

sanskrit: vigṛhyāsanam apy āhur durbalena balīyasaḥ ātmarakṣākaras tasmān na vigṛhṇīta durbalaḥ
english: "They say that even taking a position in defiance of a stronger power is self-preserving for the weak; therefore the weak should not enter into conflict."

sanskrit: yāṃ cemāṃ manyase dhātrīm etad bilam iti śrutam etal lakṣmaṇabāṇānām īṣatkāryaṃ vidāraṇe
english: "And this cave that you regard as a protective refuge — it is said that Lakṣmaṇa's arrows would make short work of tearing it open."

sanskrit: svalpaṃ hi kṛtam indreṇa kṣipatā hy aśaniṃ purā lakṣmaṇo niśitair bāṇair bhindyāt patrapuṭaṃ yathā lakṣmaṇasya ca nārācā bahavaḥ santi tadvidhāḥ
english: "Indra once accomplished little by hurling his thunderbolt; Lakṣmaṇa would split it apart with his sharp arrows as though slicing a leaf-cup, and Lakṣmaṇa has many iron-shafted arrows of that kind."

sanskrit: avasthāne yadaiva tvam āsiṣyasi paraṃtapa tadaiva harayaḥ sarve tyakṣyanti kṛtaniścayāḥ
english: "The very moment you, O afflictoer of enemies, sit down in the fast unto death, all the monkeys, their resolve firm, will abandon you."

sanskrit: smarantaḥ putradārāṇāṃ nityodvignā bubhukṣitāḥ kheditā duḥkhaśayyābhis tvāṃ kariṣyanti pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: "Remembering their sons and wives, ever anxious, hungry, worn out by uncomfortable beds, they will put you behind them."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ hīnaḥ suhṛdbhiś ca hitakāmaiś ca bandhubhiḥ tṛṇād api bhṛśodvignaḥ spandamānād bhaviṣyasi
english: "You, bereft of friends and of kinsmen who wish you well, will be fearful even of a trembling blade of grass."

sanskrit: na ca jātu na hiṃsyus tvāṃ ghorā lakṣmaṇasāyakāḥ apavṛttaṃ jighāṃsanto mahāvegā durāsadāḥ
english: "And Lakṣmaṇa's dreadful arrows, swift and irresistible, intent on killing the fugitive, will certainly pierce you."

sanskrit: asmābhis tu gataṃ sārdhaṃ vinītavad upasthitam ānupūrvyāt tu sugrīvo rājye tvāṃ sthāpayiṣyati
english: "But if you come with us, presenting yourself humbly, Sugrīva will in due course establish you in the kingdom."

sanskrit: dharmakāmaḥ pitṛvyas te prītikāmo dṛḍhavrataḥ śuciḥ satyapratijñaś ca nā tvāṃ jātu jighāṃsati
english: "Your uncle is devoted to dharma, steadfast in his vows, pure, and true to his promises; he will never seek to harm you."

sanskrit: priyakāmaś ca te mātus tadarthaṃ cāsya jīvitam tasyāpatyaṃ ca nāsty anyat tasmād aṅgada gamyatām
english: "He also desires your mother's well-being, and his very life exists for her sake; he has no other offspring. Therefore, Aṅgada, let us go."

sanskrit: śrutvā hanumato vākyaṃ praśritaṃ dharmasaṃhitam svāmisatkārasaṃyuktam aṅgado vākyam abravīt
english: Hearing Hanumān's words — modest, filled with dharma, and accompanied by due honor to his master — Aṅgada replied.

sanskrit: sthairyaṃ sarvātmanā śaucam ānṛśaṃsyam athārjavam vikramaiś caiva dhairyaṃ ca sugrīve nopapadyate
english: "Steadfastness, complete purity of soul, compassion, uprightness, valor, and courage — none of these are to be found in Sugrīva."

sanskrit: bhrātur jyeṣṭhasya yo bhāryāṃ jīvito mahiṣīṃ priyām dharmeṇa mātaraṃ yas tu svīkaroti jugupsitaḥ
english: "He who, while his elder brother yet lives, takes for himself that brother's cherished queen-wife — she who should rightfully be regarded as a mother — is contemptible."

sanskrit: kathaṃ sa dharmaṃ jānīte yena bhrātrā durātmanā yuddhāyābhiniyuktena bilasya pihitaṃ mukham
english: "How can he know dharma — that evil-souled one who, while his brother was engaged in battle, blocked the mouth of the cave?"

sanskrit: satyāt pāṇigṛhītaś ca kṛtakarmā mahāyaśāḥ vismṛto rāghavo yena sa kasya sukṛtaṃ smaret
english: "He who has forgotten Rāghava — who took his hand in truth, who has done him service, who is of great renown — whose good deed would such a one remember?"

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya bhayād yena nādharmabhayabhīruṇā ādiṣṭā mārgituṃ sītāṃ dharmam asmin kathaṃ bhavet
english: "He who, not through fear of adharma but through fear of Lakṣmaṇa alone, commanded us to search for Sītā — how can there be dharma in such a one?"

sanskrit: tasmin pāpe kṛtaghne tu smṛtihīne calātmani āryaḥ ko viśvasej jātu tat kulīno jijīviṣuḥ
english: "Who among the noble, who is well-born and desires to live, would ever trust that sinner, that ingrate, that forgetful and unstable soul?"

sanskrit: rājye putraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya saguṇo nirguṇo 'pi vā kathaṃ śatrukulīnaṃ māṃ sugrīvo jīvayiṣyati
english: "Having established his own son in the kingdom — whether that son be virtuous or not — how will Sugrīva allow me to live, born of an enemy's line?"

sanskrit: bhinnamantro 'parāddhaś ca hīnaśaktiḥ kathaṃ hy aham kiṣkindhāṃ prāpya jīveyam anātha iva durbalaḥ
english: "With my counsel betrayed, myself in transgression, and my power diminished, how could I reach Kiṣkindhā and live there, helpless and weak like an orphan?"

sanskrit: upāṃśudaṇḍena hi māṃ bandhanenopapādayet śaṭhaḥ krūro nṛśaṃsaś ca sugrīvo rājyakāraṇāt
english: "That deceitful, cruel, and pitiless Sugrīva would have me punished in secret and put in bonds, for the sake of securing his kingdom."

sanskrit: bandhanāc cāvasādān me śreyaḥ prāyopaveśanam anujānīta māṃ sarve gṛhān gacchantu vānarāḥ
english: "A fast unto death is better for me than imprisonment and degradation. Grant me leave, all of you; let the monkeys go to their homes."

sanskrit: ahaṃ vaḥ pratijānāmi na gamiṣyāmy ahaṃ purīm ihaiva prāyam āsiṣye śreyo maraṇam eva me
english: "I declare to you: I will not go to the city. I shall sit here in fast unto death; death itself is better for me."

sanskrit: abhivādanapūrvaṃ tu rājā kuśalam eva ca vācyas tato yavīyān me sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ
english: "And my younger uncle Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, should first be given my respectful salutation and then asked about his welfare."

sanskrit: ārogyapūrvaṃ kuśalaṃ vācyā mātā rumā ca me mātaraṃ caiva me tārām āśvāsayitum arhatha
english: "Ask about the good health and welfare of Rumā as well, my mother. And you should please console my mother Tārā."

sanskrit: prakṛtyā priyaputrā sā sānukrośā tapasvinī vinaṣṭaṃ mām iha śrutvā vyaktaṃ hāsyati jīvitam
english: "She is by nature devoted to her son, compassionate, a woman of many austerities; upon hearing that I have perished here, she will surely abandon her life."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ vṛddhān apy abhivādya ca saṃviveśāṅgado bhūmau rudan darbheṣu durmanāḥ
english: Having said this much and having also bowed to the elders, Aṅgada lay down upon the ground on the darbha grass, weeping and downcast in spirit.

sanskrit: tasya saṃviśatas tatra rudanto vānararṣabhāḥ nayanebhyaḥ pramumucur uṣṇaṃ vai vāriduḥkhitāḥ
english: As he lay there, the bull-like monkeys, weeping, stricken with grief, shed hot tears from their eyes.

sanskrit: sugrīvaṃ caiva nindantaḥ praśaṃsantaś ca vālinam parivāryāṅgado sarve vyavasyan prāyam āsitum
english: Blaming Sugrīva and extolling Vālin, they all surrounded Aṅgada and resolved to undertake the fast unto death.

sanskrit: mataṃ tad vāliputrasya vijñāya plavagarṣabhāḥ upaspṛśyodakaṃ sarve prāṅmukhāḥ samupāviśan dakṣiṇāgreṣu darbheṣu udaktīraṃ samāśritāḥ
english: Knowing the intention of Vālin's son, those bull-like monkeys — all having touched water, facing east, seated on southward-tipped darbha grass, on the bank of the ocean — settled down together.

sanskrit: sa saṃviśadbhir bahubhir mahīdharo mahādrikūṭapramitaiḥ plavaṃgamaiḥ
english: That mountain, as many monkeys massive as great mountain peaks lay down upon it —

sanskrit: babhūva saṃnāditanirjharāntaro bhṛśaṃ nadadbhir jaladair ivolbaṇaiḥ
english: — resounded through its ravines and cascades, as though with the violent tumult of roaring rain-clouds.
